extracted.subtask_description: Wire-service style reporting and editorial guidance about international affairs, U.N. proceedings, and the role of the press; aimed at informing (and guiding) journalists and the general public on coverage standards and international-diplomatic procedural points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of the people to know
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of protection by the American press of 'the right of the people to know.' 'If the American press becomes derelict in its devotion to the right of the people to know, or if it fails to use its freedom to let the people know, it helps to destroy freedom.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presses should treat informing the public as a core duty because public understanding underpins democratic freedom; failure to inform can assist in undermining freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present all relevant facts and context
rubrics_metrics.description: The press must present all facts about the plan, the attitudes of other nations, background conditions, arguments for and against and 'calm but vigorous editorial discussion.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage of international plans (e.g., European aid) should include factual detail, other nations' perspectives, historical/background context and balanced argumentation rather than partisan or one-sided reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify relationships and expose distortion
rubrics_metrics.description: The press also has the duty ... of making the interrelationships of facts clear, the moral obligation to expose any willful distortion and the responsibility to clarify the readers' thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should explain how facts connect, actively call out deliberate misinformation, and write to improve readers' understanding rather than obscure or inflame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the press in shaping policy (normative standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The role of the press in shaping national policy ... is an active and an essential role. For unless the people know, they cannot understand. Where there is no understanding, there is misunderstanding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial and reporting practice should recognize that press coverage can influence national policy; therefore accuracy, clarity, and responsibility are required given potential policy implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: UN Security Council voting and veto practice
rubrics_metrics.description: The council had previously approved the commission plan paragraph by paragraph ... but when it came to a final vote on the plan as a whole Gromyko used his power of veto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting or analysis of Security Council action must account for the distinction between paragraph-by-paragraph approvals and final votes, and the decisive impact of a permanent member's veto even when earlier votes passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on non-UN commissions and reporting channels
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-U.N. commission would be limited ... it could not report directly to the Security Council ... and under the charter they would not be bound to cooperate with it if established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proposing alternatives to UN bodies, note their formal limits: lack of direct reporting to the Security Council, potential constitutional/charter constraints, and possible non-cooperation by states; such limitations affect legitimacy and practical effectiveness.
